note: snapshot::check returns Missing when <memo>.tetel is not a directory, Unreadable when compose::render(&dir) errors, Matches only when the whole rendered String equals memo_source byte-for-byte, and Drifted (first differing line, both line counts) otherwise. The Provenance enum has exactly these four variants; nothing in it distinguishes which input changed.

report.rs prints Provenance::Drifted as a machine row "[provenance-drift]" whose text names two causes, "Either the document was edited by hand after rendering, or the workspace moved on without a re-render", and remedies "Re-render, or recover the workspace the text really came from." It names no cause in which the renderer itself changed. Unreadable is printed under the same "provenance-drift" row kind.

compose::render emits, in order: the prose blocks (render_prose), then render_targets, render_transplants, render_ledger and render_facts, each appended to the same String. Everything after the prose is generated by tetel from targets.jsonl, transplants.jsonl, claims.jsonl and facts.jsonl; the author supplies none of its layout.

lib.rs check_report parses the memo's own bytes (parse::parse_document(&source)) and imports the evidence ledger from that document body (ledger::import(&doc.body)); the claims every later check grades — analyze, analyze_ledger (ungrounded, disagreements, qualified, out-of-proof), grounding_provenance — are those parsed out of the rendered text, not read from the snapshot's claims.jsonl. Provenance is graded afterwards by snapshot::check(path, &source) over the same bytes.

checks.rs doc comment: every proposition_digest on record was computed over a ledger-derived proposition — the claim as rendered into the ledger table by compose::ledger_cell (embedded newlines replaced by spaces) and read back by ledger::split_row_cells (every cell trimmed) — not over claims.jsonl's text. So the bytes render emits for a ledger cell are what grading records are keyed to.

Both read the document's text in the layout the current build's parsers expect.

snapshot.rs SNAPSHOT_FILES is a fixed 10-entry array (facts, claims, prose, targets, transplants .jsonl; counters.json, pending.json, refusals.log, identity.json, acks.jsonl), and it has grown over time: targets.jsonl, transplants.jsonl, identity.json and acks.jsonl each carry a comment for when they were added, the acks.jsonl comment noting "a build predating this line never opens the file". snapshot::write copies exactly these names; pending.json is shipped although render never reads it.

buildid::label() returns "tetel <CARGO_PKG_VERSION> build <short digest of the running executable>" (or "build unidentifiable — <why>"). The digest is over the executable's bytes, so it differs between any two builds, whether or not their render output differs; it identifies a build, not a render format.

snapshot::write at the pin only copies the SNAPSHOT_FILES names present in the workspace over the snapshot directory. It never deletes anything already there, so a file it does not write (for example a render.json left by a later build) survives any render --out by this build.

Direction 2 of checks::census_findings and of checks::premise_findings reads target symbols and transplant ids out of the document body with the current build's section parsers. When a document row is not in the snapshot, each reports that the row "was not written by `tetel target`" or "…`tetel transplant`". Both functions assume the document's layout is the current renderer's.

workspace::read_jsonl returns an empty list, not an error, when the file is missing. So rendering a snapshot directory that has lost claims.jsonl or targets.jsonl succeeds and just omits those rows. A missing file does not make the snapshot Unreadable.
